evidence_map.value: AP estimated increased Latino voter support for Trump in 2024; a later Pew survey reported lower approval among Latino voters who had supported him, and the report did not establish how they would vote later.
evidence_map.basis_quote: AP estimated that Trump received about 43% of the Latino vote in 2024, up from 35% in 2020; the analysis also noted that a majority of Latino voters still supported Kamala Harris in 2024. To assess whether those gains persisted, AP cited a Pew Research Center survey from April 2026. Among Latino voters who had supported Trump in 2024, Pew found his approval had fallen from 93% near the start of his term to 66% in April. The story discussed concerns about prices, immigration enforcement and the administration’s immigration policies as possible factors shaping voters’ views. These figures describe different measures: AP’s estimates of vote choice in presidential elections and Pew’s later measure of approval among Trump’s Latino voters. They should not be read as a direct polling comparison of the same question over time. The report describes a potential political vulnerability ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, but it does not establish how those voters would ultimately vote or whether the 2024 coalition would hold.

blockers: The description distinguishes election vote estimates from a later approval measure; it does not establish that the same question was polled over time or how voters would vote in a future election.
